I've been trying to prove that a recursive function always terminates, but I've realised that there is an issue using sizeOf, as it does not aknowledge that all evaluations of a certain type must pass through a separate function.

I'm having issues summarising the issue, and since the code as a whole is quite small, I thought I might as well give it all here:

inductive DELForm (Agents : Type) (Props : Type) (Actions : Type) where
  | bot                                                     : DELForm Agents Props Actions
  | var (p : Props)                                         : DELForm Agents Props Actions
  | not (ϕ : DELForm Agents Props Actions)                  : DELForm Agents Props Actions
  | and (ϕ ψ : DELForm Agents Props Actions)                : DELForm Agents Props Actions
  | know (a : Agents) (ϕ : DELForm Agents Props Actions)    : DELForm Agents Props Actions
  | update (α : Actions) (ϕ : DELForm Agents Props Actions) : DELForm Agents Props Actions

structure DELFrame where
  agents : Type
  states : Type
  sim : agents → states → states → Prop

structure Val (States : Type) where
  props : Type
  eval : props → States → Prop

structure ActionModel (Agents : Type) (Props : Type) where
  states : Type
  sim : Agents → states → states → Prop
  pre : states → (DELForm Agents Props states)


notation (name := falsity) "⊥'" => DELForm.bot
notation (name := proposition) "v'" n:arg => DELForm.var n
notation (name := negation) "¬'" ϕ:arg => DELForm.not ϕ
notation (name := conjunction) ϕ:arg " ∧' " ψ:arg => DELForm.and ϕ ψ
notation (name := knowledge) "K'" a:arg ϕ:arg => DELForm.know a ϕ
notation (name := update) "['"α:arg"]'"ϕ:arg => DELForm.update α ϕ

notation (name := validity) "⊤'" => ¬' ⊥'
notation (name := disjunction) ϕ:arg " ∨' " ψ:arg => ¬' ((¬' ϕ) ∧' (¬' ψ))
notation (name := implication) ϕ:arg " →' " ψ:arg => ψ ∨' (¬' ϕ)


def delforces (M : DELFrame) (V : Val M.states) (AM : ActionModel M.agents V.props) :
            M.states → DELForm M.agents V.props AM.states → Prop
  | _, ⊥'       => false
  | s, (v' n)   => V.eval n s
  | s, (¬' ϕ)   => ¬ (delforces M V AM s ϕ)
  | s, (ϕ ∧' ψ) => (delforces M V AM s ϕ) ∧ (delforces M V AM s ψ)
  | s, (K' a ϕ) => ∀ t, M.sim a s t → delforces M V AM s ϕ

  | s, ['α]'⊥'       => false
  | s, ['α]'(v' n)   => delforces M V AM s (AM.pre α) → delforces M V AM s (v' n)
  | s, ['α]'(¬' ϕ)   => delforces M V AM s (AM.pre α) → ¬ (delforces M V AM s (['α]'ϕ))
  | s, ['α]'(ϕ ∧' ψ) => delforces M V AM s (['α]'ϕ) ∧ (delforces M V AM s (['α]'ψ))
  | s, ['α]'(K' a ϕ) => delforces M V AM s (AM.pre α) → ∀ β, (AM.sim a α β → delforces M V AM s (K' a (['α]'ϕ)))
  | s, ['α]'(['β]'ϕ) => delforces M V AM s (AM.pre α) → (delforces M V AM s (['β]'ϕ))

In short, the issue is that [α](v n) resolves to pre(α) → v n so I must prove that sizeOf(pre(α)) < sizeOf [α](v n). The problem here (From what I can tell) is that the pre function increases the size of α, and must always be called for α to resolve. However, sizeOf disregards that α must go through the pre function and assigns DELForm.update α (DELForm.var n) a size of 2, rather than pre(α) + 1, which I believe would be needed.
On the other hand, I could be missing something entirely trivial, who knows.

Thanks for any help - Ward.

P.S. I'm pretty sure the action composition section is wrong, but I don't think that's relevant here.
Hello! What rules out for example the case where AM.pre α := ['α]'(['α]'(⊥')), or any other complicated pre?

That's a good point! - I've been basing general semantics on a book, but missed that the language is inductively defined such that a given action α can only call existing actions within its precondition - I'll work on that, though I'm not sure if that would solve this issue aswell.
If the code above can't rule out my example, then your function does not terminate.

Okay I may have slightly lost the plot, but I believe I've now solved that issue. The Action Model now has an order on the states lt and the partial function delforces now returns a formula with a subtype of actions based on that order.
There's probably a better way of doing it, but regardless, I still have the termination issue. The only difference now is that sizeOf([α](v n)) goes to 3.
The changed code is as follows:

structure ActionModel (Agents : Type) (Props : Type) where
  states : Type

  lt : states → states → Prop
  lt_antirefl : ∀ (s : states), ¬ (lt s s)
  lt_antisymm : ∀ (s s' : states), lt s s' → ¬ (lt s' s)
  lt_trans : ∀ (s s' s'' : states), (lt s s' ∧ lt s' s'') → lt s s''

  sim : Agents → states → states → Prop
  pre : (s : states) → (DELForm Agents Props {s' : states // lt s' s})

def delforces (M : DELFrame) (V : Val M.states) (AM : ActionModel M.agents V.props) (lt : AM.states → Prop) :
            M.states → DELForm M.agents V.props (Subtype lt) → Prop
  | _, ⊥'       => false
  | s, (v' n)   => V.eval n s
  | s, (¬' ϕ)   => ¬ (delforces M V AM lt s ϕ)
  | s, (ϕ ∧' ψ) => (delforces M V AM lt s ϕ) ∧ (delforces M V AM lt s ψ)
  | s, (K' a ϕ) => ∀ t, M.sim a s t → delforces M V AM lt s ϕ

  | s, ['α]'⊥'       => false
  | s, ['α]'(v' n)   => delforces M V AM (AM.lt · α) s (AM.pre α) → delforces M V AM lt s (v' n)
  | s, ['α]'(¬' ϕ)   => delforces M V AM (AM.lt · α) s (AM.pre α) → ¬ (delforces M V AM lt s (['α]'ϕ))
  | s, ['α]'(ϕ ∧' ψ) => delforces M V AM lt s (['α]'ϕ) ∧ (delforces M V AM lt s (['α]'ψ))
  | s, ['α]'(K' a ϕ) => delforces M V AM (AM.lt · α) s (AM.pre α) → ∀ (β : Subtype lt), (AM.sim a α β → delforces M V AM lt s (K' a (['β]'ϕ)))
  | s, ['α]'(['β]'ϕ) => delforces M V AM (AM.lt · α) s (AM.pre α) → (delforces M V AM lt s (['β]'ϕ))
I'm pretty sure the same issue still exists, nothing seems to rule out my counterexample

The counterexample fails (I hope) because the type of pre(α) is DELForm Agents Props {s' : Actions // lt s' α}. By lt_antirefl, this does not include α, so it cannot appear in its own precondition. Similar is true for other actions greater than α in the heirarchy, so you can't have cyclic preconditions either.
I didn't define AM.pre α := α, so lt_antirefl doesn't rule it out

AM.pre α := [α]([α](⊥)) is shorthand for DELForm.update α (DELForm.update α (DELForm.bot)) where α is of type Actions. But the Actions type for pre(α) is {s' : Actions // lt s' α}. So α can only be in that type if lt α α, which is contradicted by lt_antirefl.
Why does AM.pre α := ['α]'(['α]'(⊥')) require lt α α?
Because pre : (s : states) → (DELForm Agents Props {s' : states // lt s' s}) so the only actions that the function can use in the returned formula are those from {s' : states // lt s' s}
Yeah but that only requires lt ['α]'(['α]'(⊥')) α, not lt α α
But that's just shorthand for DELForm.update α (DELForm.update α (DELForm.bot)), which would require α : Actions

What's wrong with it? α is of type Actions
Hang on I might be confused
The Actions in this case is the subtype {s' : states // lt s' s} of the previous case

Update: I've changed DELForm to take a whole (pointed) action model, rather than just the action. This, hopefully, will help the issue with recursion. However, I now have a new issue where pre using a subtype of Actions prevents it from being within a mutual block. On the other hand, if it didn't, I would then get the non-termination issue when recursing over the precondition where an action's precondition could call itself.

New code (Edit, removed type differnce at pre):

mutual
inductive DELForm {Actions : Type} (Agents : Type) (Props : Type) (ltα : Actions → Prop) where
  | bot                                                 : DELForm Agents Props ltα
  | var (p : Props)                                     : DELForm Agents Props ltα
  | not (ϕ : DELForm Agents Props ltα)                  : DELForm Agents Props ltα
  | and (ϕ ψ : DELForm Agents Props ltα)                : DELForm Agents Props ltα
  | know (a : Agents) (ϕ : DELForm Agents Props ltα)    : DELForm Agents Props ltα
  | update  (AMα : PointedActionModel Agents Props ltα)
            (ϕ : DELForm Agents Props ltα)              : DELForm Agents Props ltα


structure PointedActionModel {Actions : Type} (Agents : Type) (Props : Type) (ltα : Actions → Prop) where
  point : (Subtype ltα)

  lt : Actions → Actions → Prop
  lt_antirefl : ∀ (s : Actions), ¬ (lt s s)
  lt_antisymm : ∀ (s s' : Actions), lt s s' → ¬ (lt s' s)
  lt_trans    : ∀ (s s' s'' : Actions), (lt s s' ∧ lt s' s'') → lt s s''

  sim : Agents → Actions → Actions → Prop
  pre : (s : Actions) → (DELForm Agents Props (lt · s))
end

Note: I tried an equivalent representation where I passed (ltα : Actions → Prop) between the structures with {Actions : Type} , rather than (Actions : Type). This prevented the type change from Actions to Subtype Actions, but still has an issue within the mutual block. The specific error (kernel) arg #11 of 'PointedActionModel.mk' contains a non valid occurrence of the datatypes being declared.
(Edit: Updated the code to this variant)

So the fundamental issue seems to be that the structure returned by pre contains a decreasing subtype of Actions. This means that I can't include it within DELForm as the type doesn't match. On the other hand, if I don't include it, then the DELForces function can't terminate because the recursive level of something from DELForm increases after pre is used. So, if I can use some method to 'assure' DELForces that sizeOf(DELForm.update α ϕ) ≤ sizeOf(AM.pre α) + sizeOf(ϕ) (The more likely thing to fix between the two options) then I think it should work. The only issue is that I have no idea how to do that...

Quite new semantics and a new basis for (hopefully) proving recursion:
Action updates have been changed to be evaluated based on expanding the model by the actions.
I've realised the key point in proving recursion, being a measure that is strictly decreasing between iterations, is split between two objects. In most cases, the object is the formula ϕ. However, on an action update, the decreasing measure is the list of available actions ltα, which may eventually create an empty type based on Subtype ltα, another potential issue.

My issue now is in telling Lean that ltα is strictly decreasing between recursions, and that fomulas involving an empty type of Subtype ltα (Actions) is actually fine. The latter because there are paths through the inductively defined DELForm that do not use elements of type Actions. Conceptually, I believe that this would work? But I'm not really sure if it's allowed/valid.

In short, I need some form of termination_by s ϕ => sizeOf ϕ + sizeOf (Subtype ltα) but Lean complains because ltα varies between interations, which it would need to for the sizeOf function to decrease...

Nevertheless, here's the changed code:

inductive DELForm {Actions : Type} (Agents : Type) (Props : Type) (ltα : Actions → Prop) where
  | bot                                                 : DELForm Agents Props ltα
  | var (p : Props)                                     : DELForm Agents Props ltα
  | not (ϕ : DELForm Agents Props ltα)                  : DELForm Agents Props ltα
  | and (ϕ ψ : DELForm Agents Props ltα)                : DELForm Agents Props ltα
  | know (a : Agents) (ϕ : DELForm Agents Props ltα)    : DELForm Agents Props ltα
  | update  (α : Subtype ltα)
            (ϕ : DELForm Agents Props ltα)              : DELForm Agents Props ltα

structure DELFrame (Ag : Type) where
  states : Type
  sim : Ag → states → states → Prop

structure Val (Props : Type) (States : Type) where
  eval : Props → States → Prop

structure ActionModel (Ag : Type) (P : Type) where
  states : Type

  lt : states → states → Prop
  lt_antirefl : ∀ (s : states), ¬ (lt s s)
  lt_antisymm : ∀ (s s' : states), lt s s' → ¬ (lt s' s)
  lt_trans    : ∀ (s s' s'' : states), (lt s s' ∧ lt s' s'') → lt s s''

  sim : Ag → states → states → Prop
  pre : (s : states) → DELForm Ag P (lt · s)

notation (name := falsity) "⊥'" => DELForm.bot
notation (name := proposition) "v'" n:arg => DELForm.var n
notation (name := negation) "¬'" ϕ:arg => DELForm.not ϕ
notation (name := conjunction) ϕ:arg " ∧' " ψ:arg => DELForm.and ϕ ψ
notation (name := knowledge) "K'" a:arg ϕ:arg => DELForm.know a ϕ
notation (name := update) "['"α:arg"]'"ϕ:arg => DELForm.update α ϕ

notation (name := validity) "⊤'" => ¬' ⊥'
notation (name := disjunction) ϕ:arg " ∨' " ψ:arg => ¬' ((¬' ϕ) ∧' (¬' ψ))
notation (name := implication) ϕ:arg " →' " ψ:arg => ψ ∨' (¬' ϕ)

def DELFrame.expand {Props : Type} {Agents : Type}
                    (M : DELFrame Agents) (AM : ActionModel Agents Props) :
                     DELFrame Agents where
  states := (M.states × AM.states)
  sim := fun a ((s, s') : M.states × AM.states) ((t, t') : M.states × AM.states) =>
          (M.sim a s t) ∧ (AM.sim a s' t')

def Val.expand {Agents : Type} {Props : Type} {States : Type}
               (V : Val Props States) (AM : ActionModel Agents Props) :
                Val Props (States × AM.states) where
  eval := fun (p : Props) ((s, _) : (States × AM.states)) => V.eval p s


def delforces {Ag : Type} {Props : Type}
              (M : DELFrame Ag) (V : Val Props M.states) (AM : ActionModel Ag Props) (ltα : AM.states → Prop) :
               M.states → DELForm Ag Props ltα → Prop
  | _, ⊥'       => false
  | s, (v' n)   => V.eval n s
  | s, (¬' ϕ)   => ¬ (delforces M V AM ltα s ϕ)
  | s, (ϕ ∧' ψ) => (delforces M V AM ltα s ϕ) ∧ (delforces M V AM ltα s ψ)
  | s, (K' a ϕ) => ∀ t, M.sim a s t → delforces M V AM ltα s ϕ
  | s, ['α]'ϕ   => delforces M V AM (AM.lt · α) s (AM.pre α) →
                    ∀ s' : AM.states, delforces (M.expand AM) (V.expand AM) AM ltα (s, s') ϕ

Moving on / Minimal Working Example

I'll be moving on from this to work on other stuff, so as a send off I'm giving a minimal(-ish) working example of the issue I'm coming across:

inductive Formula {Act : Type} (P : Type) (ltα : Act → Prop) where
  | bot                                           : Formula P ltα
  | not (ϕ : Formula P ltα)                       : Formula P ltα
  | exp (α : Act) (h : ltα α) (ϕ : Formula P ltα) : Formula P ltα

structure AM (Act : Type) (P : Type) where
  lt : Act → Act → Prop
  lt_antirefl : ∀ (s : Act), ¬ (lt s s)
  lt_antisymm : ∀ (s s' : Act), lt s s' → ¬ (lt s' s)
  lt_trans    : ∀ (s s' s'' : Act), (lt s' s ∧ lt s'' s') → lt s'' s

  pre : (s : Act) → Formula P (lt · s)

def forces {Act : Type} {P : Type} (V : Act → Prop) (Am : AM Act P)
            (ltα : Act → Prop) (h : ∃ a : Act, ltα = (Am.lt · a)) : Formula P ltα → Prop
  | Formula.bot         => False
  | Formula.not ϕ       => ¬ forces V Am ltα h ϕ
  | Formula.exp α h' ϕ  => forces V Am (Am.lt · α) (by exists α) (Am.pre α)

The issue here is that while not is decreasing the size of ϕ, exp is decreasing the size of Subtype ltα. At the same time, it arbitrarily increases the size of ϕ through pre.
This should be provably terminating based on the axioms of lt within AM giving an order to Act that exp is moving through. Nevertheless, since ltα isn't fixed, Lean complains that it won't terminate.
That's all from me, though if I ever figure out how to prove termination I'll update this.

Your counterexample only fails to terminate because you had b < a rather than a < b, which meant the Formula.exp case was putting α in the wrong spot. In the same vein, you were putting (s + 1) in the precondition of s, which would imply, when lt is the right way around, by the definition of pre, that s + 1 < s.

Okay that took way longer than it should have, but despite learning somewhat about Fintypes and Finsets, my conclusion was that it was much easier to have

  lt_close : ∀ s' : Act, (∃ s : Act, lt s s') →

Conclusion:
It (the non-MWE) terminates! Indeed, the proof was a lot smaller than that in the end.
It uses two key points: Termination is lexicographically ordered where the first entry is ~ the number of available actions, and the second the size of ϕ.
The main issue here is that the 'number of available actions' isn't deducible with only a wellfounded relation, since it isn't finite (So you can't create a sizeOf instance). You have to use IsWellFounded.rank to create an ordering, then prove that this rank is necessarily smaller when an ActionModel points at an action lower in ranking than another (Done using IsWellFounded.rank_lt_of_rel).
At this point, you can show all non-update cases terminate as normal, while the update case terminates based on this proof.
